correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and connection to the depicted upper river
correspondence.finding: The CEHQ original does not depict a continuous watercourse through the chosen western opening. The next eastward reach converges on its mapped upper Manitou, but the omitted link cannot be inferred. Archambault describes a poorly defined northwestern headwater network; this is regional context only.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Manitou valley and approach to the first large lake
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward turn and subsequent southward bends follow the depicted, labeled Manitou corridor toward Lac Manitou. Adjacent western lake-fed and eastern Magpie routes remain distinct.

correspondence.component_scope: Lac Manitou approach, longitudinal passage and southern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected path enters the long north-south lake and continues through its southern outlet. The lake label is separate from the river label; western neighboring Lac Tortue is not substituted for this passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Inter-lake southward corridor, eastern bend and western return
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the connected southward, southeastward and returning westward corridor. Broadened intermediate waters remain unnamed here; no tributary or lake name is supplied from proximity alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Lac des Eudistes passage and southern outlet vicinity
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern-side passage reaches the depicted southern lake outlet and lower river. Lac des Eudistes retains its distinct identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Manitou descent and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The CEHQ river line follows the selected lower descent toward the Saint-Laurent coast. Archambault describes the lower falls and a triangular estuary. These support the receiving coastal setting without identifying the selected endpoint as an exact mouth or tidal boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected final point and estuarine connection
correspondence.finding: The final selected point lies on the mapped coastal approach before the generalized coastline. The inspected admissible cartography does not distinguish its relation to the estuary entrance and downstream outlet. A modeled sea-terminal class is not used as physical-source proof.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern_chosen_opening
correspondence.finding: The entire eastern chosen headward part, including its turn toward the west, lacks independently read cartographic correspondence. No source proves its name or connection to a named receiving lake/channel.

correspondence.component_scope: upper_westward_parts
correspondence.finding: All seven westward selected parts, potential lake passages, and inter-part receiving links remain unestablished from source cartography. The model route supplies orientation only.

correspondence.component_scope: upper_southern_bend
correspondence.finding: The southwestern bend and subsequent northward parts remain unestablished. Nearby or remembered lake names are not assigned; actual through-lake and outlet links have not been observed.

correspondence.component_scope: northward_middle_parts
correspondence.finding: All nine northward/northwestern selected parts and any intermediate lake or tributary joins remain without source correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: westward_receiving_join
correspondence.finding: The westward middle corridor, its southwest bend, and receiving-trunk transition lack independent map evidence. No single river name is extended across the modeled junction.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_westward_corridor
correspondence.finding: All14 downstream selected parts through the northern bend and westward lower corridor remain unestablished from cartography. No present hydraulic connection or component hydronym is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: coastal_approach_and_fragment_join
correspondence.finding: The final three parts of the larger fragment and their link to FID9240 require source evidence. A modeled adjacency is not proof of the actual coastal connection.

correspondence.component_scope: actual_selected_terminal
correspondence.finding: The separate terminal fragment requires ordinary-scale proof of the actual river-mouth/fjord or coastal link. No receiving fjord name, precise mouth, or current shoreline is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen glaciated opening and first approach to Angle Creek
correspondence.finding: The actual chosen opening is within the blue-stippled glaciated terrain southeast of the mapped Angle Creek headward channel. The selection proceeds northwest across the ice and ice-margin setting before meeting the channel network. Original cartography depicts the glacier, adjacent relief and streams beyond its margin, but does not depict a watercourse establishing the full selected opening across the ice. Glacier proximity, topographic descent and model connectivity are insufficient to infer a mapped surface or subglacial hydraulic link. The glacier is not assigned a name.

correspondence.component_scope: Angle Creek upper valley, braided reach and southward joining reach
correspondence.finding: Beyond the initial glaciated passage, repeated Angle Creek labels and connected mapped channels establish the westward upper valley, broad braided reach and lower southwest-turning channel. The source distinguishes nearby Windy Creek and the River Lethe drainage on the eastern side of the relief. Angle Creek continues through its lower bends into the separate Takayofo Creek channel. Minor unnamed feeders, braid branches and nearby small lakes retain their distinct component scope; no individual braid is selected as the current active channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Takayofo Creek and Contact Creek joining setting
correspondence.finding: The selected westward route follows the separately labelled Takayofo Creek below the Angle Creek junction. The mapped Contact Creek channel approaches from the north and joins this westward river. The downstream channel is repeatedly labelled King Salmon River. These original mapped connections establish the tributary-to-receiving-river transition; they do not establish an exact legal name-change vertex. Contact Creek is a distinct incoming tributary, not a selected headwater name.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper King Salmon River and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The King Salmon River proceeds west along the mapped valley, turns northwest and enters a broad braided corridor. The Gertrude Creek approach from the south and Granite Creek approach from the north are separately labelled, and their joining settings are visible in the continuous river network. The selected geometry simplifies bends, but the original establishes the same receiving-river corridor and through-connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Central braided King Salmon River corridor
correspondence.finding: Overlapping originals show the named King Salmon River continuing west and northwest through interconnected braided channels and islands. Numerous small lakes and wetland areas lie beside the river. The selected main corridor remains within the continuous mapped river valley and does not require an unsupported lake-to-lake or cross-wetland transfer. Side lakes are not renamed as King Salmon River.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle river bends and lake-rich surroundings
correspondence.finding: The named river continues through successive broad bends, local channel divisions and the western boundary surroundings of Becharof National Wildlife Refuge. The original depicts the channel links themselves across this entire interval. Adjacent lakes and ponds are separate side waterbodies; no selected through-lake passage or reservoir is shown in this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower braided river and southwest transition
correspondence.finding: The two western originals overlap across the lower braided reach and establish its continuous transition into the wider, more sinuous southwest-flowing King Salmon River. Nearby floodplain lakes, abandoned-looking loops and small side channels are distinguished from the selected through-corridor. The generalized selection clips local meanders, without creating a regional through-link gap in the inspected mapped river.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower King Salmon estuarine reach and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the final King Salmon River bends widening into a lower estuarine reach beside King Salmon Island. The actual rendered endpoint lies at the eastern margin surroundings of that lower King Salmon reach, north of the island and upstream of the visible joining area with the separately labelled Egegik River. The Egegik River and settlement provide receiving-estuary context, but the selected endpoint is not relocated to their junction, a more distant bay mouth or the open sea. A precise bank, tidal line, distributary choice or legal river-mouth boundary is not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual southeastern opening, southwestward reach and southern turn
correspondence.finding: The supplied path begins east of the main southern lagoon district and turns southwest before its southern return. Figure32 is a generalized rural-study location map and does not delineate the chosen opening or its connection into the long northward selected reach. The RP11 satellite panels do not cover this southern opening. No lagoon or channel name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern turn and long straight northward corridor
correspondence.finding: The pinned parts are long, nearly north-south segments. The rural map and prose supply a regional lagoon/drainage setting but do not continuously register these particular segments as a mapped channel, canal or connected water route. Straight modeled geometry alone does not establish a drainage-work identity. The southern link and any intervening lagoon passage remain unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern middle corridor and short connecting bends
correspondence.finding: The available rural-study map is too generalized to establish the chosen series of local bends and joins. Regional drainage descriptions cannot distinguish this selected strand from adjacent roads, drains or wetland channels. No named component is supported for the full selected interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward eastern approach and northern westward turn
correspondence.finding: The inspected historical images show the low-lying drainage landscape around the RP11 and General Lavalle area. They lack a selected-route registration or a sufficiently clear continuous depiction of these parts. The regional distinction between an estuarine outlet and the separate coastal saltmarsh outlet cannot be used to choose the selected transfer between them.

correspondence.component_scope: Long southward return west of the preceding selected strand
correspondence.finding: This southward return is materially distinct from the preceding northward reach. Neither the rural map nor the limited historical satellite panels establishes the full return, its southern reversal or its connection to the next northward strand. Named neighboring drainage and report-wide regional flow descriptions do not supply these links.

correspondence.component_scope: Western northward corridor and final coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The available sources identify multiple managed and natural drainage components at regional scale, but their specific correspondence to this western selected strand remains unestablished. No continuous source path across its joins, sluices or wetland transitions is demonstrated. Historical sluice descriptions are not current operating evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected northern terminal, including its final short adjustment
correspondence.finding: The rural map provides broader bay and estuarine context. The historical satellite panels concentrate around the road corridor and do not resolve the actual selected terminal at the outer coastal end. A regional receiving-water name or a modeled sea-terminal classification is insufficient to prove the selected final connection. No mouth or saltmarsh-channel identity is assigned.
